item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I actually don't mind the ending; I know he's supposed to be superhuman to a point, but frankly it always felt more silly to me that he can tank multiple large-caliber BMG rounds to the head and keep functioning enough to be a threat. I get that 682 can do that because he's a regenerating alien eldritch lizard thing (Toffee, maybe?), but Able is technically still a human. I get that being so hard to kill is part of what makes him threatening, but once a person loses a large enough portion of brain, they really shouldn't be able to keep going.

I do enjoy this story, Crow, and I do hope you keep it.

item.title: Re: Is there a Plot hole?
item.content:encoded:
A somewhat lengthy explanation.
 [R1] Hide, Ashley

Well, the first and last two points you raised could be explained (In a somewhat lenient manner, that is), by this segment:

The man glared at her, fury growing at this effrontery. Those who had come before had been weaklings, but they had at least been warriors of a sort.

From this, we can infer that 076-2 simply doesn't acknowledges Langley as a threat, disregarding the possibility that any of his inhuman acrobatics would be needed in order to finish off such a frail "opponent". Sure, it's certainly debatable whether or not a shaken, untrained researcher would be able to take a shot under such mental strain, but it wouldn't be accurate to rule out this possibility either, given Able's recklessness.

That being said, let's take a look at SCP-076 main page:

Take multiple .50 caliber BMG rounds to the head and survive for several minutes to continue killing, despite severe damage to the cerebellum.

So, Able will continue to move after getting hit in the head by several of these things, which were likely fired from a modern equivalent of this little thing, but immediately drop dead after being shot once by a pistol. Umm.

TL;DR: Given that this is a tale, stories in which improbable things happen quite often, it's hardly fair to qualify this particular situation as a plot hole, but it's certainly iffy to assume that Langley, besides hitting Able in a lucky shot, would also be casually carrying around some kind of super OTT handgun capable of outclassing heavy MG's by such large, unrealistic margin.

item.title: Is there a Plot hole?
item.content:encoded:
Interesting, but I feel like there's a plot hole.

How could the doctor, contain/kill Able like that with the following:

  • Able could have evaded the bullet
  • Able could have parried the bullet
  • I'm not sure about this but, Able could withstand more punishment even from a headshot.
  • The gun being too big to aim accurately
  • The doctor too shaky to aim it accurately

I know this is kinda an old tale. But I really like it except that little plot hole

item.title: Re:

I think he likes what she could become. It's all about the potential with that man. But considering her current willingness to fight, or lack thereof, he might resent her more than he does the others, because she has something, and isn't using it to the fullest.

Those who aren't willing to give their all would disgust him almost as much as total non-combatants.

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
Thanks Grey. I have no idea as to how to finish it, but I did want to demonstrate his impotence with regards to everyone thinking he's overpowered. A bullet to the head kills him just as easily as anyone else.

Though I think he gets kinda emo-y at the middle and stuff, and there's little other things that just kinda bug me.

Oh, and for the detail about his day, I kinda wanted to imply that ninety percent of the time, he didn't have anything of interest to do, and that one of his major problems is that he's going even crazier from boredom, because he's stuck in a place he hates, with people he hates, in a world that he would probably find more interesting if it was on fire.

But yeah, more stuff would be kinda better from a reading point of view.
